citation: docs/mip/0004-agent-messaging.md, sections 2 to 5 and 13, and its table of what council v1 got wrong
why: What the message service does is a function of its participants, their groups, the logs and cursors, and whose inbox still answers, so it is data: each case is a script of steps by named callers, and each step is answered with one line. A caller is a Claude session (`session`, whose inbox socket is /tmp/cc-socks/<session>.sock), a name given with --as (`as`), or neither, which is the human. `dies` makes a session's inbox stop answering. Groups number their entries from 1, and creating one logs `created` and the creator's join before anything else.

cases.name: an unaddressed post wakes every member but its author
cases.why: The default policy's ring set is every member, and an author is never woken by its own post (MIP-4, section 5).

said: a posted #5 to g; woke b [g #5-5 x1 to-you:0 from a], c [g #5-5 x1 to-you:0 from a]

cases.name: an addressed post wakes only its addressees, and every member can still read it
cases.why: Council v1 released every waiter at once when a post named a departed agent. Addressing decides who is woken, never who may read: there are no private messages (MIP-4, Decision 2).

said: a posted #5 to g; woke b [g #5-5 x1 to-you:1 from a]
c read g: #5 a->b: take the lexer

cases.name: a participant is woken once per batch, and again only after it reads
cases.why: Ten messages arriving while an agent works cost it one wake; every wake it acts on is a turn it pays for (MIP-4, section 5).

said: a posted #4 to g; woke b [g #4-4 x1 to-you:0 from a]
a posted #5 to g; already woken b
b read g: #4 a: one | #5 a: two
a posted #6 to g; woke b [g #6-6 x1 to-you:0 from a]

cases.name: the guard refuses a post while its author has unread messages
cases.why: The stale-context guard from council v1: a post is refused until its author has read what others posted there, and there is no override (MIP-4, section 4).

said: a posted #4 to g; woke b [g #4-4 x1 to-you:0 from a]
b posted #5 to g; woke a [g #5-5 x1 to-you:0 from b]

cases.name: joins do not count as unread
cases.why: Council v1's lock counted joins, so every join made every pending post stale (MIP-4, section 4).

said: a posted #5 to g; woke b [g #5-5 x1 to-you:0 from a], c [g #5-5 x1 to-you:0 from a]

cases.name: a participant whose inbox is gone is not woken
cases.why: A wake address is found dead at first use and marks its participant gone until it returns (MIP-4, sections 5 and 12).

said: a posted #5 to g; woke b [g #5-5 x1 to-you:0 from a]; gone c
a posted #6 to g; already woken b; gone c
a alive, b alive, c gone

cases.name: read shows others' messages and notices, never the reader's own
cases.why: Reading back one's own post would count as noise; a notice about someone else is how a member learns the group changed (MIP-4, section 4).

said: a posted #4 to g; woke b [g #4-4 x1 to-you:0 from a]

cases.name: a post to agents who share no group creates the group of exactly them
cases.why: Two agents can message each other without convening anything, and there is still one kind of log (MIP-4, section 2).

said: a posted #4 to a+b; woke b [a+b #4-4 x1 to-you:1 from a]
b posted #5 to a+b; woke a [a+b #5-5 x1 to-you:1 from b]

cases.name: a post goes to the one group its author and addressees share
cases.why: Members of a council messaging each other stay under the council's policy (MIP-4, section 2).

said: a posted #4 to g; woke b [g #4-4 x1 to-you:1 from a]

cases.name: a post that fits several groups is refused until it names one
cases.why: Guessing between two groups would put a message under the wrong policy and in the wrong log (MIP-4, section 2).

said: a posted #4 to h; woke b [h #4-4 x1 to-you:1 from a]

cases.name: an unaddressed post from a caller in no group is refused
cases.why: An unaddressed post goes to its author's group, and a caller in none has no group to post to (MIP-4, section 2).

cases.name: joining under a gone participant's name takes it over, cursors included
cases.why: A resumed agent has new addresses; taking over its old name keeps what it had read, and a live holder of the name is never displaced (MIP-4, section 3).

said: builder posted #4 to g; gone critic
critic read g: #3 builder joined | #4 builder: while you were away

cases.name: a caller that never named itself is named after its directory
cases.why: Parallel sessions sit in worktrees of their own, so the directory is the name a person would use; a second session there gets a suffix, and a new session takes over a name whose session is gone (MIP-4, Open Questions, answered in stage 1).

cases.name: a caller with no agent identity is the human, who waits for messages rather than being woken
cases.why: A person's own shell has no agent identity, and messages to the human wait for them; nothing wakes the human until attention routing does (MIP-4, sections 3 and 10).

said: @human read g: #3 a joined | #4 a->@human: need input

cases.name: a wait returns when a waking message arrives, and a newer wait ends the older
cases.why: wait is what a hook runs in the background; at most one runs per participant (MIP-4, section 13).

said: a posted #4 to g; woke b [g #4-4 x1 to-you:0 from a]
ready g #4-4 x1 to-you:0 from a

cases.name: a post is refused when it addresses someone it cannot reach there
cases.why: Each refusal names what is wrong, so the agent can fix the post rather than guess (MIP-4, section 2).

cases.name: leaving a group is a notice in its log, and leaving everything stops being a participant
cases.why: Joins and leaves are part of the transcript a late joiner reads (MIP-4, sections 4 and 13).

said: #1 created by a | #2 a joined | #3 b joined | #4 b left | #5 a: anyone?

cases.name: a newcomer's reading starts when it joins, and the log still holds what came before
cases.why: History from before a join is what log is for; counting it as unread would refuse the newcomer's first post (MIP-4, section 4).

said: a posted #4 to g; woke b [g #4-4 x1 to-you:0 from a]
c posted #6 to g; woke a [g #6-6 x1 to-you:0 from c]; already woken b
#4 a: early | #5 c joined | #6 c: hello

cases.name: a name must be one a command line and a log can carry
cases.why: Names appear in commands, notices and file names, so they are letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen (MIP-4, section 11 for why they must be unique).

cases.name: a group whose name differs from another's only in case is refused
cases.why: On a filesystem that ignores case, which is macOS's default, two such groups would share one log file and merge after a restart; a person would not tell them apart either (MIP-4, section 12).

cases.name: a group name is short enough to be a file name
cases.why: Each group's log is a file named after it, and a file name has at most 255 bytes (MIP-4, section 12).

cases.name: a post to so many that their group's name would be too long is refused
cases.why: A post to agents who share no group creates the group of exactly them, named after them; past the length a group name may be, the author has to make a group and name it (MIP-4, sections 2 and 12).

cases.name: a session cannot act as a live participant it is not
cases.why: join --name refuses the name of a live participant, and --as on any verb is held to the same rule: otherwise a mistyped --as moves that participant's inbox to the caller, and the real one is never woken again. A caller with no session of its own, such as a script, may act as it without moving anything (MIP-4, section 3).

cases.name: a session that takes over a name is woken, whatever the old one was told
cases.why: A wake went to the old session, which exited before reading; the session that comes back under its name has been woken for nothing yet (MIP-4, section 3, Coming back).

said: director posted #4 to g; woke builder [g #4-4 x1 to-you:0 from director]
director posted #5 to g; woke builder [g #4-5 x2 to-you:0 from director]

cases.name: joining under a default name that a gone session held says it took over
cases.why: A resumed session in the same directory comes back under its old name, cursors included, and is told so as it would be with --name (MIP-4, section 3).

cases.name: the human's wait is answered by a post for the human
cases.why: Nothing wakes the human's window until attention routing does, but a person's script waiting on a message is a wait like any other (MIP-4, sections 10 and 13).

said: a posted #4 to g; woke @human [g #4-4 x1 to-you:1 from a]

cases.name: leaving ends the leaver's wait, or one it kept to the group it left
cases.why: A wait whose participant has left can never be answered, and holds the daemon's thread until its caller hangs up (MIP-4, section 13).

cases.name: a session that never took part is told so, not called the human
cases.why: The refusal names the caller as it asked; a Claude session that never ran a msg command has no name yet (MIP-4, section 3).

cases.name: an agent in a pane is addressed by its pane before it has run any command
cases.why: An agent started by `muster pane new --run claude` has joined nothing, and a brief to it is the first message; a post to its pane makes it a participant, named after the pane, and it is rung there. When it runs a command from that pane it is that participant (MIP-4, sections 3 and 14).

said: integrator posted #4 to integrator+p1; woke p1 [integrator+p1 #4-4 x1 to-you:1 from integrator] rung p1
p1 posted #5 to integrator+p1; woke integrator [integrator+p1 #5-5 x1 to-you:1 from p1]

cases.name: a pane with no agent in it is no address, and a shell there is the human
cases.why: A person's own shell in a pane has no agent identity; only a pane where an agent has been found can be addressed or identify its caller (MIP-4, section 3).

cases.name: an agent in a pane is rung there, even when it also has an inbox
cases.why: A session that bypasses permission prompts holds an inbox message for a person's approval, which is how agents in panes are started, and the daemon cannot tell which sessions do (MIP-4, section 6).

said: a posted #4 to g; woke b [g #4-4 x1 to-you:0 from a] rung p1

cases.name: an agent that goes idle without reading is woken once more, and not again
cases.why: A wake may land while an agent is busy with something it then finishes; one more, saying the messages are still unread, and then nothing until it reads (MIP-4, section 5).

said: a posted #4 to g; woke b [g #4-4 x1 to-you:0 from a] rung p1
rewoke b [g #4-4 x1 to-you:0 from a again] rung p1
b read g: #3 a joined | #4 a: one
a posted #5 to g; woke b [g #5-5 x1 to-you:0 from a] rung p1
rewoke b [g #5-5 x1 to-you:0 from a again] rung p1

cases.name: an agent whose pane has lost its agent is gone
cases.why: A pane closing, or detection seeing its agent exit, is how a pane participant leaves without saying so (MIP-4, section 7).
